children: YIELDS, OIL AND TECH DRAG ON U.S. STOCKS WITH RATE HIKE IN SIGHT

Wall Street's three major indexes ended Tuesday's session lower with pressure from rallying oil prices and rising bond yields in the last full session before the Federal Reserve is widely expected to raise interest rates.
And on the industry level, technology
was a big drag for the second straight day after leaders in artificial intelligence called for a slowdown in development in order to keep AI under human control.
U.S. crude oil futures

settled up 4.38%, or $4.44, at $105.83 for their fourth straight finish above $100 after shipping industry sources said oil loadings at Saudi Arabia's Red Sea port of Yanbu had been suspended, and Libya halted operations at three oil fields, fueling concerns that disruptions to key oil supply routes could persist for weeks. Brent
, the international benchmark, settled up $3.07 at $108.75.
With traders pricing in a 94.5% probability, as per CME Group, for a rate hike after the Fed's meeting finishes on Wednesday, benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury note yields
were hovering close to 5% after earlier hitting their highest levels since 2007.
Among the S&P 500's 11 major industry sectors, technology was the second-biggest weight behind consumer discretionary
, while energy
brought the biggest boost with support from rising oil prices. Consumer discretionary fell 1.8% while energy rose 2.3%. Heavyweight tech fell just 0.3%, but represented 9.7% of index point declines.
In individual stocks, the biggest drag came from Microsoft

, which fell 1.6%. On Monday, the software giant had unveiled an in-house development code of conduct that would require its AI to never resist correction or shutdown, to communicate so humans can understand, and to consider any conduct violation as a failure.
AI chip leader and market heavyweight Nvidia
was the biggest boost, but its 0.6% advance followed a 3.4% drop in the prior session. The PHLX semiconductor index
edged up 0.4% on Tuesday after a 5.9% tumble on Monday.
Here is your closing snapshot:
Main US equity indexes end lower; Nasdaq leads losses, down ~0.8%
Consumer Discretionary is weakest S&P 500 sector; energy leads gainers
Dollar gains; US crude settles up >4%; gold ~flat; bitcoin falls >4%
US 10-year Treasury yield hits 5.041%, highest since 2007, now ~5.01%
